abstract: Vertical asymmetry generally precludes accidental bound states in the continuum (BICs) in planar photonic lattices, yet the underlying physical mechanism remains unclear. In this study, we show that accidental-BIC formation is governed by the definite parity of the transverse radiation-source profile rather than by geometric vertical mirror symmetry. A semianalytical coupled-mode analysis shows that an accidental BIC occurs when the radiation overlap integral of a leaky Bloch mode vanishes. We decompose the overlap into contributions from the even- and odd-parity components of the transverse radiation-source profile. Complete radiation suppression requires both contributions to vanish simultaneously. In vertically symmetric lattices, the source profile has definite even or odd parity, causing one contribution to vanish identically. Thickness tuning can null the remaining contribution and produce an accidental BIC. In vertically asymmetric lattices, by contrast, both parity components are generally present. The waveguide dispersion forbids their simultaneous vanishing, thereby precluding an accidental BIC. Introducing a parity-restoring layer into a vertically asymmetric lattice restores definite parity to the transverse radiation-source profile, thereby enabling the formation of an accidental BIC. Finite-element simulations confirm the analytically predicted recovery of accidental BICs for both TE$_0$ and TE$_1$ Bloch modes.
